explain.say: On Earth, a feather floats down slowly while a hammer drops fast. That's because the air pushes back on the wide, light feather much more than on the heavy hammer.

explain.say: Galileo had predicted this centuries earlier: without air, all things fall at the same rate. A heavier object is pulled harder, but it is also harder to get moving, so the two effects cancel.

faq.q: What happened in the hammer and feather experiment?
faq.a: On 2 August 1971, Apollo 15 commander David Scott dropped a hammer and a falcon feather on the Moon. They fell side by side and landed at the same time, showing Galileo was right.
asks: Who dropped a feather on the Moon?

faq.q: Why did they land together on the Moon?
faq.a: The Moon has no air, so there was no air resistance to slow the feather. Only gravity acted, and gravity gives all objects the same acceleration.
asks: Why is there no air resistance on the Moon?

faq.q: Why does a heavy object not fall faster?
faq.a: Gravity pulls a heavy object harder, but a heavy object also needs a bigger force to speed it up. The two effects cancel exactly, so all objects speed up at the same rate.

faq.q: How fast do things fall on the Moon?
faq.a: The Moon's gravity is about one sixth of Earth's, so things speed up more slowly there, gaining about 1.6 metres per second every second. The hammer and feather both fell this gently.
asks: Is falling slower on the Moon?

faq.q: Can you do the experiment on Earth?
faq.a: Yes, in a vacuum chamber with the air pumped out. In one famous film at a huge NASA vacuum chamber in Ohio, a bowling ball and feathers were dropped together and landed together.
asks: Has the feather test been done in a vacuum?

facts: Apollo 15 commander David Scott performed the hammer and feather drop on the Moon on 2 August 1971.
Gravity on the Moon is about 1.62 metres per second squared, about one sixth of Earth's.
The feather Scott dropped was a falcon feather, a nod to the name of his lunar module, Falcon.

quiz.say: On the Moon, an astronaut drops a hammer and a feather together. What happens?
quiz.show: On the Moon, a hammer and a feather dropped together…
quiz.why: With no air on the Moon, only gravity acts, and it speeds up every object at the same rate.

wrong.1: That happens on Earth because of air; the Moon has none.
wrong.2: The Moon's gravity pulls the feather down like everything else.
